597203.old: A patient pulled from a house fire can have both carbon monoxide and cyanide (from burning plastics and foam) in the blood. CO occupies hemoglobin so O2 is not delivered; cyanide binds the iron of cytochrome c oxidase so the O2 that does arrive cannot be used. In both cases the tissues switch to anaerobic glycolysis and blood lactate rises, causing metabolic acidosis. High-flow oxygen helps displace CO from hemoglobin; for cyanide the antidote hydroxocobalamin (a form of vitamin B12) binds the cyanide ion so it can be excreted as cyanocobalamin, because more oxygen alone cannot unblock the enzyme.

CO occupies hemoglobin, so O2 is not delivered; cyanide blocks cytochrome c oxidase, so the O2 that does arrive cannot be used (Molecule in the Clinic, above). Either way the tissues switch to anaerobic glycolysis and blood lactate rises, causing metabolic acidosis. High-flow oxygen helps displace CO from hemoglobin, but more oxygen alone cannot unblock the enzyme, which is why cyanide needs its own antidote.

597209.old:
Unsaturated fatty acids

Unsaturated fatty acids have \(\ce{C=C}\) bond in their alkyl chain. \(\beta\)-Oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids happens the same way as for saturated fatty acids except for the following changes. If \(\ce{C=C}\) bond is a trans-\(\ce{C=C}\) bond between \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) \(\ce{C's}\), reaction 1 in the \(\beta\)-oxidation is not needed and \(\ce{FADH2}\) from reaction 1 is not produced. If \(\ce{C=C}\) bond is a cis-\(\ce{C=C}\) bond or it is between \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\) \(\ce{C's}\), it goes through isomerization reactions catalyzed by isomerase enzymes to convert the \(\ce{C=C}\) bond into a trans \(\ce{C=C}\) bond between \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) \(\ce{C's}\) before reaction 2 happens on it. Unsaturated fatty acids yield a little less \(\ce{ATP's}\) due to one \(\ce{FADH2}\) less produced per \(\ce{C=C}\) bond, but the difference is small and the formula: \((7\times{n}-6)~\ce{ATP's}\), still gives a reasonably accurate estimate of \(\ce{ATP}\) yield.
